n.1: Oral complaints must also be accepted.
n.2: Outsourcing needs oversight; responsibility stays with the firm.

11.q: Which action demonstrates limiting behaviour to compliance?
o: Requiring fairness metrics in staff reviews
11.w: Rigidly following templates without judgement reflects compliance-limited thinking rather than ethics.

n.0: Adapting for vulnerability shows ethics beyond compliance.
n.2: Fairness metrics reflect an ethical culture.
n.3: Proactive disclosure is an ethical indicator.

11.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
11.q: Why must adviser Mona consider a client's sustainability preferences under ESG rules?
o: ESG funds will always outperform others
ESG preferences replace the full fact-find
The client may prioritise ESG factors
11.w: Clients may value sustainability, so Mona must record and integrate ESG preferences into the suitability assessment.

n.0: not guaranteed by ESG
n.1: preferences complement fact-finding
n.2: suitability still applies

11.q: At the international level, which standard-setter is responsible for issuing the Basel banking accords?
o: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
11.w: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision issues the Basel Accords, setting international standards for bank capital and risk.

n.1: The International Monetary Fund supports global stability but issues no accords.
n.2: The European Central Bank sets eurozone monetary policy, not prudential standards.
n.3: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development focuses on economic policy, not banking regulation.

11.q: Which of the following best describes the FCA's enforcement powers?
o: It can only issue guidance carrying no penalties
It can impose fines, censures and restrictions
It prosecutes every criminal offence itself
Its role is limited to mediating disputes
11.w: The FCA's enforcement powers include fines, public censures, banning individuals, and restricting firms' activities.

n.0: The FCA can penalise breaches, not merely guide.
n.2: It refers most serious criminal cases to other authorities.
n.3: Dispute mediation is the FOS's role, not enforcement.

11.q: Which situation would most likely give rise to a constructive trust?
o: Property held for another out of fairness
Two parties signing a deed of trust
A settlor transferring assets into a trust
11.w: Constructive trusts are imposed by courts to prevent unfairness, where it would be inequitable for one party to keep sole benefit.

n.1: A deed of trust creates an express trust.
n.2: A settlor creating a trust makes an express trust.
n.3: Executors distribute under a will, not a constructive trust.

11.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
11.q: A client shows limited financial literacy during a meeting. What must adviser Rosa do?
o: Ignore the gap and carry on as normal
Cut the fact-find down to simplify it
Rely only on the product brochures
11.w: Rosa should tailor her communication and provide additional support so the client can make an informed decision.

n.1: risks unsuitable advice
n.2: undermines the suitability assessment
n.3: cannot ensure understanding

11.q: At the start of a meeting, adviser Julia spends time putting a nervous client at ease. What is the purpose of building this rapport?
o: To establish trust and open communication
To avoid having to prepare any documentation
To remove the need for objectives
11.w: Rapport fosters trust and openness, encouraging clients to share objectives and concerns fully, which supports suitability.

n.1: Rapport does not exempt from compliance.
n.2: Documentation is still needed.
n.3: Objectives remain central.

11.q: Adviser Zoe advises both first-time savers and experienced investors. Why must she adapt her communication style to each?
o: Clients vary in knowledge and preferences
It exempts her from disclosure duties
It removes the need for suitability reports
11.w: Different clients need simpler explanations or technical detail, so adapting communication helps all clients understand and choose informedly.

n.0: Communication style cannot guarantee returns.
n.2: Disclosure remains mandatory.
n.3: Suitability reports are still required.

11.q: Why must identified conflicts of interest be recorded and mitigated before a firm conducts annual discretionary reviews?
11.w: Principle 8 requires managing conflicts to prevent detriment and protect client interests before decisions are taken.

n.0: cross-selling focuses on revenue, not protection
n.1: tax filing is unrelated to conflicts
n.2: speed is operational, not the purpose

11.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
11.q: During a review, adviser Priya notices signs of vulnerability but the client declines any additional support. What must Priya do?
o: Record the refusal and the reasons
11.w: Priya should document the refusal and its rationale to evidence that needs were considered, consistent with Consumer Duty.

n.0: disproportionate; the duty is to consider needs, not cease advice
n.1: vulnerability does not change categorisation
n.3: reasonable aids should remain available

11.q: Which FCA principle requires firms to pay due regard to the interests of their customers?
11.w: Principle 6 requires firms to pay due regard to customers' interests and treat them fairly.

n.0: Principle 1 concerns integrity.
n.1: Principle 4 relates to financial resources.
n.2: Principle 9 concerns suitability for customers relying on the firm's judgment.

11.q: A client holds shares through a bare trust and asks how the trustees may act. Which statement is correct?
o: Trustees actively manage the assets with full discretion
Trustees hold legal title, acting as beneficiaries direct
Trustees acquire beneficial ownership alongside legal title
The trust itself owns the assets as a legal entity
11.w: In a bare trust, trustees hold legal title but must act on the directions of beneficiaries, who hold the entire beneficial interest.

n.0: Full discretion describes a discretionary trust, not a bare trust.
n.2: Trustees hold legal title only, not beneficial ownership.
n.3: A trust is not itself a separate legal entity.

11.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
11.q: Client Tara has just inherited a substantial sum. What must her adviser do in response?
o: Ignore it until the annual review
Review her goals, capacity and strategy
Reclassify her as a professional client
11.w: A significant inheritance alters affordability, objectives and risk capacity, so the plan should be reviewed and adapted.

n.0: Delay risks unsuitable advice.
n.1: Growth cannot be guaranteed.
n.3: More wealth does not change categorisation.

11.q: What must firms do under the Consumer Duty price and value outcome?
11.w: The price and value outcome requires firms to evidence that total price represents fair value given the benefits delivered.

n.1: Competitor pricing is not the benchmark.
n.2: Charges need not be lowest, only fair for benefits.
n.3: Adviser pay is not prohibited.

11.q: Which UK legislation gives regulators powers to tackle money laundering offences?
11.w: The Money Laundering Regulations 2017 provide the framework for regulators, including the FCA, to supervise and enforce AML compliance.

n.0: The Banking Act deals with bank resolution, not AML.
n.1: The Companies Act concerns company law, not AML.
n.2: The FS Act 2012 addresses market abuse, not AML specifically.

11.q: How does the FCA’s strategic objective interact with its operational objectives?
o: Operational objectives override the strategic one
Operational objectives deliver the strategic aim
The strategic objective is optional guidance
The strategic objective applies only in crises
11.w: The operational objectives of consumer protection, competition and integrity deliver the strategic aim of markets functioning well.

n.0: The strategic objective sets the framework and is not overridden.
n.2: It is statutory, not optional.
n.3: It applies continuously, not only in crises.

11.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to have effective risk management strategies?
11.w: Fundamental Rule 5 requires firms to have effective risk strategies and risk management systems suited to their business.

n.0: Fundamental Rule 2 requires diligence, not risk strategies.
n.2: Fundamental Rule 4 requires resources, not risk systems.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 8 concerns resolution, not risk strategies.

11.q: Which FCA Principle requires a firm to observe proper standards of market conduct?
11.w: Principle 5 requires firms to observe proper standards of market conduct.

n.0: Principle 2 covers diligence, not market conduct.
n.1: Principle 6 concerns fair treatment, not market conduct.
n.2: Principle 9 concerns suitability, not market conduct.

11.q: What is a key reason for prioritising saving for children's education?
o: It exempts parents from FCA rules
It guarantees a higher salary for the child
It prepares for predictable future costs
11.w: Education savings help families meet foreseeable expenses, avoiding future borrowing or financial stress.

n.0: FCA rules govern firms, not family saving.
n.1: Inheritance tax is unaffected by education saving.
n.2: Saving cannot guarantee a child's future salary.

11.q: A firm must show a dilemma was managed appropriately. Which documentation provides the strongest evidence?
o: A verbal assurance from the adviser
A list of the adviser's client referrals
11.w: A compliance-reviewed record with rationale demonstrates transparency, fairness and accountability.

n.0: Verbal assurance cannot be evidenced.
n.1: Sales summaries show no ethics.
n.3: Referral lists are operational.

11.q: A 16-year-old dies intestate in England and Wales. How is the estate treated?
o: It is automatically forfeited to the Crown
It passes to their parents or guardians
It is held in trust for their siblings
It is shared equally between friends and relatives
11.w: A minor cannot make a valid will, so on death the estate is distributed under intestacy, usually to the parents.

n.0: The Crown inherits only where no relatives survive.
n.2: Siblings do not inherit before parents.
n.3: Friends are not recognised under intestacy.

11.q: What is the PRA’s approach to setting requirements for an insurer’s own funds?
o: Risk-based standards aligned to Solvency II
A uniform leverage ratio identical to retail banks
Product intervention capping premiums for vulnerable customers
11.w: For insurers the PRA applies a risk-based prudential regime aligned to Solvency II concepts, focusing on policyholder protection and firm soundness.

n.1: A bank-style leverage ratio is not applied uniformly to insurers.
n.2: Premium caps are a conduct matter.
n.3: Monetary policy tools sit with the MPC.

11.q: A client holds an existing enduring power of attorney (EPA). Which statement most accurately describes it?
o: It is identical to an ordinary power of attorney
It remains valid after loss of capacity, if registered
It can only be used for health and welfare decisions
It becomes automatically invalid after the donor's death
11.w: EPAs, created before their replacement by LPAs, continue after incapacity provided they are registered with the OPG.

n.0: Ordinary powers end on incapacity; EPAs survive it.
n.2: EPAs cover property and financial affairs, not welfare.
n.3: Like all attorneys' powers, an EPA ends on death, not by rule of invalidity here.

11.q: An adviser recommends a trust giving a surviving spouse income for life while preserving capital for the children. Which trust is this?
11.w: A life interest trust gives the beneficiary, often a spouse, income for life while preserving the capital for others, such as children.

n.0: A discretionary trust gives trustees flexibility, not a fixed life interest.
n.2: A protective trust restricts access on bankruptcy.
n.3: A bare trust gives absolute entitlement.

11.q: What is meant by the FCA's approach to risk-based supervision?
o: All firms are supervised in an identical manner
Only firms with consumer complaints are supervised
Supervision is delegated entirely to HM Treasury
11.w: Under a risk-based approach the FCA allocates supervisory resources according to the impact and probability of harm a firm poses.

n.1: Supervision is proportionate to risk, not identical.
n.2: Complaints are only one factor among many.
n.3: HM Treasury sets policy; the FCA retains supervision.

11.q: Which Bank of England body sets system-wide macroprudential policy?
o: The Court of the Bank of England
11.w: Macroprudential policy, such as sectoral capital requirements and the countercyclical buffer, is set by the Financial Policy Committee to address system-wide risks.

n.0: The PRC oversees firm-level prudential regulation.
n.2: The MPC targets price stability through monetary policy.
n.3: The Court is the Bank’s governing board.

11.q: Which FCA principle requires firms to take reasonable care to ensure the suitability of investment decisions for their clients?
11.w: Principle 9 requires firms to take reasonable care to ensure the suitability of advice and discretionary decisions for clients relying on them.

n.0: Principle 2 requires skill and diligence generally.
n.1: Principle 4 relates to financial resources.
n.2: Principle 6 covers fair treatment.

11.q: Why does FSMA 2000 require clarity in the statutory objectives of regulators?
o: To let regulators replace fiscal policy
To reduce the number of regulated firms
To let regulators set tax rates
11.w: Clarity in objectives makes regulators accountable to Parliament and transparent to the public.

n.0: Regulators do not replace fiscal policy.
n.1: Reducing firm numbers is not the purpose.
n.3: Taxation is outside regulators' remit.

11.q: Which obligation does the Senior Managers Regime place on individuals holding prescribed responsibilities?
o: Delegating legal liability to junior staff
Clear accountability for their control area
Automatic exemption from routine FCA supervision
A reduced duty of integrity given seniority
11.w: The SMR gives senior managers clear accountability for their area, so regulators can trace responsibility for failures.

n.0: Liability cannot be delegated to junior staff.
n.2: FCA supervision applies to senior managers too.
n.3: Integrity duties rise, not fall, with seniority.

11.q: Why is the FCA required to balance its consumer protection objective with other objectives?
o: To centralise all authority under Treasury
To let the PRA supervise conduct
11.w: Balancing objectives keeps consumer protection from undermining competition or integrity, delivering proportionate regulation.

n.0: Zero losses is impossible.
n.1: Authority is divided, not centralised.
n.3: The PRA does not supervise conduct.

11.q: What role does the Government play in taxation of financial services?
o: It directly supervises market trading behaviour
It guarantees investment returns in ISAs
It sets tax policy on saving and investment
It manages the prudential ratios of banks
11.w: Through ISA allowances, pension tax relief and stamp duties, the Government shapes consumer and institutional behaviour in the sector.

n.0: Market conduct is the FCA's role, not tax policy.
n.1: ISA returns are not guaranteed by the Government.
n.3: Banking ratios are managed by the PRA, not tax policy.

11.q: Why was the FCA created as a separate regulator from the PRA?
o: To replace HM Treasury's fiscal role
To separate conduct from prudential regulation
To duplicate the Bank of England's core functions
11.w: The FCA focuses on conduct regulation while the PRA concentrates on prudential supervision, giving clearer accountability.

n.0: Fiscal policy stays with HM Treasury.
n.2: The FCA complements, not duplicates, the Bank.
n.3: Monetary policy remains the MPC's.

11.q: What is the effect if a complainant accepts a Financial Ombudsman Service decision?
o: It remains voluntary for the firm
It is reviewed by the FCA
It is referred automatically to court
11.w: Once the complainant accepts a FOS decision it becomes binding on both parties and is enforceable in court.

n.0: acceptance makes it binding
n.1: the FCA does not review FOS decisions
n.2: court involvement arises only to enforce

11.q: A supervisor looks for genuinely ethical behaviour, not mere compliance. Which indicator best reflects this?
o: Weighing client interests in unclear cases
Following only the minimum disclosure rules
11.w: Acting with integrity for clients where the rules are silent shows ethics beyond compliance.

n.1: Minimum disclosure is basic compliance.
n.2: Avoiding fines is reactive compliance.
n.3: This shows dependency on rules.

11.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
11.q: Adviser Ben books regular review meetings with his client Chloe. What is the main reason these ongoing reviews are necessary?
o: They remove the need for suitability reports
Client circumstances and markets can change
They exempt him from disclosure duties
11.w: Reviews keep plans aligned with changing client objectives, circumstances and market conditions, maintaining suitability.

n.0: Suitability reports are still required.
n.2: Reviews cannot guarantee performance.
n.3: Disclosure duties continue regardless.

11.q: Adviser Ken faces an ethical dilemma he cannot resolve alone. Which escalation route is most appropriate?
o: Asking peers informally on social media
Ignoring it to protect the relationship
11.w: Compliance or an ethics committee provides structured review aligned with regulatory expectations.

n.1: Social media advice is not reliable.
n.2: Proceeding ignores the dilemma.
n.3: Ignoring undermines ethics.

11.q: How does the UK Government influence financial stability through legislation?
o: By setting daily rates for banks
By passing Acts defining regulators' powers
11.w: FSMA 2000 and later reforms give regulators their statutory basis, underpinning oversight of financial stability.

n.0: Bank rates are set by banks, influenced by the Bank of England.
n.1: Equity is issued by companies, not by Government.
n.3: Accounting standards are developed by the IASB and FRC.

11.q: How does the FCA’s competition objective support innovation?
o: Letting new firms and products enter
11.w: Promoting competition lets new entrants and products challenge incumbents, fostering innovation in consumers' interests.

n.1: Regulation does not guarantee profits.
n.2: Uniform standards limit the variety innovation needs.
n.3: Restricting choice undermines competition.

11.q: Which FCA principle requires firms to observe proper standards of market conduct?
11.w: Principle 5 requires firms to observe proper standards of market conduct, supporting confidence in markets.

n.0: Principle 3 relates to organisation and risk management.
n.2: Principle 6 concerns treating customers fairly.
n.3: Principle 9 concerns customers in relationships of trust.

11.q: What is the maximum administrative fine under UK GDPR for the most serious breaches?
o: £10 million or 2% of the firm's UK turnover
11.w: The most serious UK GDPR breaches can attract fines up to £17.5m or 4% of annual worldwide turnover, whichever is higher.

n.0: This describes the lower tier, not the maximum.
n.2: £5 million is not a GDPR cap.
n.3: £1 million is too low for serious breaches.

11.q: Why should consumers consider inflation when prioritising financial needs?
o: Because it guarantees higher nominal returns
Because it erodes savings' real value
Because it removes any need for diversification
11.w: Inflation reduces purchasing power over time, so long-term plans must allow for it in saving and investment.

n.0: Inflation raises costs; it does not guarantee returns.
n.2: Diversification still matters in inflationary times.
n.3: Regulatory reporting is unaffected by inflation.

11.q: Which FCA Principle requires firms to deal with regulators openly and cooperatively?
11.w: Principle 11 requires firms to deal with regulators openly, disclosing anything of which they would reasonably expect notice.

n.0: Principle 2 concerns diligence, not regulator cooperation.
n.1: Principle 7 covers client communications, not regulators.
n.3: Principle 9 deals with suitability of advice, not regulators.

11.q: Which statutory framework defines the FCA’s and PRA’s objectives?
11.w: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, as amended, sets out the statutory objectives of both the FCA and the PRA.

n.0: The Companies Act governs company law.
n.1: The Criminal Justice Act 1993 covers insider dealing.
n.3: The Consumer Rights Act covers consumer contracts.

11.q: Which UK regulator primarily supervises anti-money laundering compliance?
11.w: The FCA supervises anti-money laundering compliance for authorised firms under the Money Laundering Regulations.

n.0: The PRA oversees prudential soundness, not AML.
n.2: The Bank of England sets monetary policy.
n.3: The CMA enforces competition law, not AML.

11.q: How do stock exchanges contribute to the functioning of the economy?
o: Provide a market to raise capital
Set minimum rates for commercial lending
11.w: Stock exchanges enable capital raising through listings and offer a secondary market for trading, improving liquidity and capital allocation.

n.0: Consumer protection is the remit of the FCA, not exchanges.
n.2: Rates are set by monetary policy and banks, not exchanges.
n.3: Deposit guarantees are provided by the FSCS, not exchanges.

11.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
11.q: Why must adviser Anya assess the tax implications of a recommendation?
o: Tax can materially affect client outcomes
Tax removes the need for a risk assessment
Tax on its own guarantees product suitability
11.w: Tax treatment can significantly change the net benefit, so it must feed into the suitability assessment.

n.1: categorisation is not based on tax
n.2: risk assessment is still needed
n.3: tax alone cannot ensure suitability

11.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to have effective governance arrangements, with a clear organisational structure?
11.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 6 requires firms to organise and control their affairs responsibly, including governance and adequate resources.

n.0: Fundamental Rule 2 requires diligence.
n.1: Fundamental Rule 4 relates to resources.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 5 concerns risk strategies.

11.q: What must firms provide regulators under SM&CR when breaches occur?
o: Only their audited annual financial statements
Proof of the firm's share-price stability
Their annual marketing and campaign strategies
Evidence of steps taken by senior managers
11.w: Firms must show that senior managers took reasonable steps in their area to prevent or address the breach.

n.0: Financial statements are separate filings.
n.1: Share price is irrelevant to breach accountability.
n.2: Marketing strategies are not relevant evidence.

11.q: How does the PRA determine which firms to supervise most intensively?
o: By assessing their impact on financial stability
By supervising every single firm to the same degree
By monitoring only firms operating overseas
By selecting firms at random each year
11.w: The PRA applies a judgement-based approach, intensifying supervision for firms whose failure would most threaten stability.

n.1: Intensity reflects systemic importance, not equal treatment.
n.2: Domestic firms can also be systemically important.
n.3: Random selection would not meet prudential objectives.

11.q: What is the total FSCS deposit protection for a joint account held by two people?
11.w: Each holder has £85,000 of cover, so a two-person joint account is protected up to £170,000.

n.0: the per-person limit, which is doubled for two holders
n.1: not the FSCS deposit limit
n.2: reflects four holders, not two

11.q: Company directors manipulate valuation data to present a stronger solvency position. Which Principle 1 obligation is breached?
11.w: Principle 1 requires integrity; manipulating valuation data undermines honesty and fairness in conduct.

n.1: prudence concerns adequate resources, not honesty
n.2: this covers systems, whereas falsification breaches integrity
n.3: conflicts management is separate from misreporting

11.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
11.q: What is the purpose of reassessing a client's affordability at each review?
11.w: Affordability reviews check that contributions and commitments remain sustainable, protecting clients from financial detriment.

n.0: Affordability is not linked to adviser pay.
n.2: Consumer Duty still applies.
n.3: Performance cannot be guaranteed.

11.q: What obligation arises under Principle 7 when a firm advertises complex structured products to retail clients?
o: Keep communications clear, fair and not misleading
Provide guaranteed monthly dividends regardless of performance
Exclude the warnings to simplify the materials
Target only professional investors, not retail
11.w: Principle 7 obliges firms to make communications clear, fair and not misleading, which matters especially for complex products.

n.1: guaranteed dividends are not required
n.2: omitting warnings would mislead clients
n.3: the duty applies to all communications

11.q: What document sets out the PRA's expectations for firms' risk management and governance?
11.w: The PRA Rulebook contains binding rules and supervisory expectations on governance and risk management.

n.0: The FCA Handbook deals mainly with conduct.
n.1: FSCS guidance relates to compensation.
n.3: MiFID II is EU investment-services law.

11.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
11.q: At each periodic review adviser Emma reassesses her client's attitude to risk. Why is repeating this assessment necessary?
o: It exempts her from meeting Consumer Duty rules
11.w: Clients' situations and attitudes evolve; reassessing risk tolerance keeps advice suitable and aligned with objectives.

n.1: Risk tolerance does not guarantee returns.
n.2: Objectives and risk tolerance are both needed.
n.3: Consumer Duty applies regardless.

11.q: What is the time limit for consumers to refer complaints to the FOS after receiving a firm's final response?
11.w: Consumers have six months from the firm's final response letter to refer a complaint to the FOS.

n.0: Three months is too short.
n.1: One year exceeds the limit.
n.3: Two weeks is far too short.

11.q: Which FCA operational objective is most relevant to preventing misleading financial promotions?
11.w: Misleading promotions undermine consumer protection, making the consumer protection objective most relevant.

n.1: Market integrity focuses on systemic confidence.
n.2: Competition concerns market dynamics.
n.3: Prudential safety concerns firm soundness.

11.q: What is the primary financial need addressed by life assurance?
11.w: Life assurance ensures dependants receive financial support on the policyholder's death, protecting household stability.

n.1: Life assurance is not a guaranteed-growth investment.
n.2: Emergency needs require liquid savings, not assurance.
n.3: Budgeting is still needed alongside cover.

11.q: What financial need is met by income protection insurance?
11.w: Income protection provides regular payments when a consumer cannot work due to illness or disability.

n.0: It replaces income, not provides investment returns.
n.1: It is for essential stability, not luxury spending.
n.3: FCA oversight continues regardless of cover.

11.q: What type of sanctions can regulators apply to individuals guilty of insider dealing?
11.w: Insider dealing attracts civil sanctions under FCA rules and criminal sanctions under the Criminal Justice Act 1993.

n.1: Warnings alone would not deter insider dealing.
n.2: Training is not a sanction for insider dealing.
n.3: Restitution is not the primary sanction.

11.q: Which Bank of England committee identifies systemic risks and takes macroprudential action?
11.w: The Financial Policy Committee identifies systemic risks and implements macroprudential policy to safeguard financial stability.

n.0: The PRC handles firm-level prudential supervision.
n.2: The MPC focuses on inflation and interest rates.
n.3: The Risk and Audit Committee oversees internal Bank controls.

11.q: Why do many plans prioritise life assurance for parents with young children?
o: To replace pensions as the main savings tool
To exempt families from inheritance tax
To secure dependants if a parent dies
11.w: Life assurance provides a lump sum or income if a parent dies, keeping the household financially secure.

n.0: Life assurance is protection, not a savings substitute.
n.1: It is not an investment product for profit.
n.2: Inheritance tax may still apply.

11.q: What is the primary economic purpose of insurance services?
o: Set interest rates across the economy
11.w: Insurance lets individuals and businesses transfer risk to insurers, pooling resources so unexpected losses are absorbed collectively.

n.0: Interest rates are set by central banks, not insurers.
n.2: Exchange rates are driven by markets, not insurers.
n.3: Monetary stimulus is a central bank role, not insurers.

11.q: An agent contracts without authority, and the principal later refuses to accept the deal. Which principle explains why the principal is not bound?
11.w: If the principal refuses to ratify, the contract remains unauthorised and does not bind the principal.

n.0: Privity restricts enforcement to the parties, not ratification.
n.1: Consideration relates to enforceability, not ratification.
n.3: Survivorship is a property concept, not agency law.

11.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
11.q: After a review, adviser Ian records the changes he and his client agreed. What is the main purpose of documenting these agreed changes?
o: To evidence ongoing suitability and compliance
To remove the adviser's disclosure obligations entirely
11.w: Recording agreed changes shows adjustments were made to maintain suitability, supporting compliance and transparency.

n.1: Documentation does not replace annual reviews.
n.2: Disclosure is still required.
n.3: Performance cannot be guaranteed.

11.q: How should a firm act under Principle 2 when developing a new algorithmic trading strategy?
o: By outsourcing all oversight to vendors
With due skill, care and diligence
11.w: Principle 2 requires the firm to apply skill, care and diligence, ensuring strategies are well designed, tested and controlled.

n.0: outsourcing oversight removes accountability
n.1: marketing speed does not replace diligence
n.3: skipping stress tests undermines diligence

11.q: Why does embedding ethical principles in staff reviews show ethics?
o: Because it guarantees maximum quarterly profits
Because it values fairness, not just rules
Because regulators require annual ethical reviews
Because it replaces all compliance monitoring
11.w: Embedding fairness in reviews ensures staff are assessed on ethical outcomes beyond the rules.

n.0: Profit is not guaranteed by fairness reviews.
n.2: Regulators do not mandate annual ethical reviews.
n.3: Compliance monitoring remains necessary.

11.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
11.q: When recommending a switch from one investment to another, what must adviser Ben document?
o: Why the new investment is more suitable
That the switch earns higher adviser fees
That the client's preferences are irrelevant
That the previous provider approved it
11.w: A switch must be justified by a documented rationale showing the new investment is more suitable than the existing one.

n.1: fees must not drive the advice
n.2: preferences remain central
n.3: not a substitute for assessment

12.q: Which insolvency process is designed to maximise creditor returns while giving a viable company a chance to survive?
12.w: Administration protects a company from enforcement while a strategy is pursued to rescue it or maximise creditor returns.

n.0: Liquidation focuses on dissolving the company.
n.2: Receivership benefits only the appointing creditor.
n.3: Bankruptcy applies to individuals.

12.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
12.q: Client Farah tells her adviser she now needs her invested funds in three years rather than fifteen. What should the adviser do about the portfolio?
o: Review and adjust its risk level
Move everything into cash at once
Reclassify her as a professional client
12.w: A shorter horizon reduces capacity for volatility, so risk should be reassessed and possibly lowered to keep advice suitable.

n.0: Liquidity can be managed but not guaranteed.
n.2: Full cash may not match her objectives.
n.3: Time horizon does not affect categorisation.

12.q: Which of the following is an example of a civil sanction the FCA may impose?
12.w: Civil sanctions include financial penalties, censures and restrictions, whereas imprisonment and prosecutions are criminal.

n.0: Imprisonment is a criminal sanction, not civil.
n.2: Confiscation orders are criminal under POCA.
n.3: CJA 1993 prosecutions are criminal, not civil.

12.q: To which body is a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) submitted?
12.w: SARs are submitted to the National Crime Agency, the UK's financial intelligence unit.

n.0: The FCA supervises conduct.
n.1: HM Treasury sets policy.
n.3: The Bank of England oversees monetary policy.

12.q: Which organisation investigates company insolvencies in the UK?
12.w: The Insolvency Service investigates insolvencies and director misconduct, supporting the UK insolvency regime.

n.0: The FCA regulates conduct, not insolvency.
n.1: The PRA supervises financial soundness.
n.2: The CMA deals with competition.

12.q: Who prosecutes market misconduct that amounts to serious criminal fraud beyond FCA enforcement?
12.w: The Serious Fraud Office can prosecute market misconduct where it constitutes serious criminal fraud beyond FCA regulatory action.

n.0: The Information Commissioner's Office enforces data protection, not financial crime.
n.2: The Financial Reporting Council regulates audits and reporting, not market crime.
n.3: The Prudential Regulation Authority focuses on prudential supervision, not criminal law.

12.q: Adviser Wendy now delivers much of her advice by video call. Why is adaptability valuable when advising remotely?
o: It removes the need for recordkeeping
12.w: Remote advice needs different techniques, such as using digital tools well, so clients still understand and engage with recommendations.

n.0: Adaptability cannot guarantee returns.
n.2: Disclosure obligations remain.
n.3: Records must always be kept.

12.q: Which of the following best explains the role of CREST in UK markets?
12.w: CREST is the UK's electronic settlement system for equities and gilts, operated by Euroclear UK & International.

n.0: bonds are issued by the DMO
n.2: insurance conduct is the FCA's role
n.3: fiscal policy is HM Treasury's role

12.q: How does the Government influence consumer confidence in financial services?
o: Set corporate bond prices in the market
Legislate for conduct rules and compensation
12.w: The Government underpins trust by creating regulators like the FCA and establishing statutory protections such as the FSCS.

n.0: The Government does not guarantee returns; risk lies with investors.
n.1: Bond prices are set by markets, not the Government.
n.3: Derivatives are regulated by the FCA, not the Government.

12.q: How do building societies contribute to the UK economy?
12.w: Building societies are mutuals focused on savings and mortgage lending, supporting home ownership and retail banking competition.

n.0: Wholesale markets are regulated by the FCA, not building societies.
n.2: Government debt is issued by the DMO, not building societies.
n.3: The Bank Rate is set by the Bank of England, not building societies.

12.q: Which body oversees monetary stability in the UK?
12.w: The Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee manages monetary stability, mainly by setting interest rates to control inflation.

n.0: The FCA oversees conduct and market integrity.
n.1: The PRA manages prudential soundness.
n.2: The CMA enforces competition policy.

12.q: Why must adviser Quentin develop strong report-writing skills when preparing recommendations for his clients?
o: Reports exempt him from disclosure duties
Reports remove the need for fact-finding
Suitability reports must be clear and compliant
12.w: Report-writing skills ensure suitability reports explain recommendations clearly, meeting regulatory requirements and informing clients.

n.0: Approval is not guaranteed.
n.1: Disclosure obligations remain.
n.2: Fact-finding cannot be replaced.

12.q: Which FCA Principle requires firms to arrange adequate protection for clients' assets when responsible for them?
12.w: Principle 10 requires firms to arrange adequate protection for clients' assets when they are responsible for them.

n.0: Principle 2 covers diligence, not asset protection.
n.1: Principle 4 covers financial resources, not client assets.
n.2: Principle 8 covers conflicts of interest, not client assets.

12.q: Which regulator is directly accountable to Parliament for its statutory objectives?
o: Both the FCA and the PRA
12.w: Both the FCA and PRA are independent regulators accountable to Parliament for achieving their statutory objectives.

n.0: The PRA is also accountable, not just the FCA.
n.1: The FCA is also accountable.
n.2: Accountability extends to the PRA and FCA separately.

12.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
12.q: Client Aisha has been diagnosed with a serious illness affecting her ability to work. What is her adviser's duty?
o: Guarantee investment returns to cover her medical costs
Ignore it until the annual review
Urgently review affordability, risk and protection
12.w: Serious illness can change affordability, risk profile and protection needs, so the plan must be reviewed urgently to stay suitable.

n.0: Performance cannot be guaranteed.
n.1: Waiting risks unsuitable advice.
n.3: Increasing equity exposure would be inappropriate.

12.q: A settlor places assets in a discretionary trust for her grandchildren. How is ownership of those assets best described?
o: Beneficiaries hold both legal and beneficial ownership
The settlor retains legal ownership after creating the trust
Trustees acquire both legal and beneficial ownership
Trustees hold legal title; rights depend on discretion
12.w: Trustees hold legal title, while beneficiaries only have a right to be considered for distributions at the trustees' discretion.

n.0: Beneficiaries lack fixed beneficial ownership in a discretionary trust.
n.1: The settlor usually gives up ownership on creating the trust.
n.2: Trustees administer, not beneficially own, the assets.

12.q: A firm designs remuneration in a way that drives churning of client portfolios. Which Principle applies?
12.w: Principle 6 requires treating customers fairly, breached by remuneration that encourages churning to clients' detriment.

n.0: systems matter, but the harm arises under fair treatment
n.2: communications must be clear, but this concerns fairness
n.3: this safeguards custody, not portfolio churning

12.q: Under SM&CR, what is the function of the Certification Regime?
o: To confirm staff are fit and proper
To register new products with the FCA
To approve the firm's financial promotions
To appoint the firm's statutory auditors
12.w: The Certification Regime requires firms to assess, at least annually, that individuals in roles capable of significant harm are fit and proper.

n.1: Product registration is not part of certification.
n.2: Promotions approval is a compliance function.
n.3: Auditors are appointed separately.

12.q: Under the FCA Principles for Businesses, which principle relates to a firm’s responsibility to maintain adequate risk management systems?
12.w: Principle 3 requires firms to organise and control their affairs responsibly and effectively, with adequate risk management systems.

n.0: Principle 1 concerns integrity.
n.2: Principle 7 concerns client communications.
n.3: Principle 10 concerns protecting client assets.

12.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
12.q: A client's capacity for loss has increased significantly since the last review. How should the adviser respond?
o: Ignore it until the next review
Reassess whether higher risk is now suitable
Switch automatically into higher-risk leveraged products
12.w: A greater capacity for loss may allow adjusted strategies, but suitability must still be demonstrated.

n.0: Ignoring it risks unsuitable advice.
n.2: Leveraged products may still be unsuitable.
n.3: Fact-finding must stay comprehensive.

12.q: How must firms handle product governance reviews?
o: Delegate reviews to unregulated third parties
12.w: Ongoing governance reviews ensure products continue to meet the needs and characteristics of the target market.

n.0: Outsourcing without oversight breaches responsibility.
n.2: Waiting for complaints is reactive, not compliant.
n.3: Firms must review their own products, not competitors'.

12.q: Under AML rules, what is a politically exposed person (PEP)?
o: A person who has defaulted on a mortgage
Someone with a prominent public function
Any director of a UK company
A client with an adverse credit history
12.w: A PEP is someone entrusted with a prominent public function, such as a senior politician, posing higher AML risk.

n.0: A mortgage default is a credit issue, not PEP status.
n.2: Company directors are not PEPs by default.
n.3: Adverse credit does not make someone a PEP.

12.q: What is the maximum criminal sentence for insider dealing under the CJA 1993?
o: Two years and a capped fine
Only financial penalties, with no imprisonment
Seven years and/or an unlimited fine
12.w: The Criminal Justice Act 1993 sets a maximum of seven years' imprisonment and/or an unlimited fine for insider dealing.

n.0: The maximum is higher than two years.
n.1: A ban is regulatory, not the statutory criminal maximum.
n.2: Imprisonment is a core sanction under the Act.

12.q: Why does the FCA’s competition objective explicitly refer to the interests of consumers?
o: To limit the PRA's prudential oversight
To let the FCA set fiscal policy
12.w: Framing competition around consumers ensures it promotes innovation, choice and fair pricing for end-users.

n.0: Profitability is not a regulatory aim.
n.1: FCA objectives do not restrict the PRA's role.
n.3: Fiscal policy is HM Treasury's remit.

12.q: Which FCA principle requires firms to take reasonable care to ensure the suitability of their advice and discretionary decisions?
12.w: Principle 9 requires firms to take reasonable care to ensure the suitability of advice and discretionary decisions for customers relying on their judgment.

n.0: Principle 2 covers skill, care and diligence generally.
n.2: Principle 3 requires adequate organisation and risk systems.
n.3: Principle 7 concerns client communications.

12.q: What outcome requires firms to support consumers throughout the product lifecycle?
12.w: The consumer support outcome requires firms to give helpful, responsive support so customers realise benefits over time.

n.1: Understanding targets communications clarity, not lifecycle support.
n.2: Price and value concerns fairness of charges.
n.3: Products and services focuses on design and targeting.

12.q: Which lawful basis under UK GDPR permits processing personal data to fulfil contractual obligations?
12.w: Processing is lawful where necessary for the performance of a contract with the data subject.

n.1: Legitimate interests involve a balancing test.
n.2: Consent is not needed where a contract requires processing.
n.3: Legal obligation covers compliance with law.

12.q: What is the purpose of the PRA’s safety and soundness objective?
o: To guarantee a profit on investments
To ensure firms don't threaten stability
To set interest rates for households
To provide insurance cover to depositors
12.w: The safety and soundness objective ensures PRA-authorised firms operate so as to reduce the risk of systemic disruption.

n.0: Profits cannot be guaranteed.
n.2: Interest rates are set by the MPC.
n.3: Deposit protection is provided via the FSCS.

12.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
12.q: Why is regular rebalancing recommended when adviser Max manages a client's portfolio?
o: To keep it aligned with the risk profile
To guarantee higher returns every year
To end the need for suitability reporting
12.w: Rebalancing keeps the portfolio reflecting the client's agreed risk profile and objectives over time.

n.1: returns cannot be guaranteed
n.2: reporting is still required
n.3: not secured by rebalancing

12.q: Which FCA initiative replaced Treating Customers Fairly with broader obligations?
12.w: Consumer Duty expands on TCF, imposing higher standards across products, price, communications and support.

n.0: Basel III concerns bank capital, not consumer outcomes.
n.1: MiFID II covers market conduct, not the overarching Duty.
n.3: Solvency II applies to insurers' prudential standards.

12.q: Which is a lawful basis for processing sensitive 'special category' data under UK GDPR?
12.w: Special category data, such as health or biometric data, needs explicit consent or another specific UK GDPR condition.

n.0: Contractual necessity alone does not permit special category processing.
n.2: Marketing interest is insufficient for sensitive data.
n.3: Automatic collection without a basis breaches UK GDPR.

12.q: After a complaint against him is upheld, Adviser Marcus reviews how he handled the case to improve. What is the main benefit of reflective practice for advisers?
o: It helps advisers learn from past cases
It replaces the firm's compliance obligations
It exempts advisers from annual reviews
12.w: Reflective practice lets advisers review previous situations, identify lessons and enhance their skills, improving service quality.

n.0: performance cannot be guaranteed
n.2: compliance obligations remain in place
n.3: annual reviews are still required

12.q: A couple appoint a guardian in their wills. What is that guardian’s role?
o: To care for the couple’s minor children
To manage the trust property for the beneficiaries
To distribute the estate’s assets among its creditors
To draft later amendments to the wills
12.w: A guardian appointed in a will is responsible for the care of minor children if both parents die while the children are under 18.

n.1: Trustees, not guardians, manage trust property.
n.2: Executors distribute estate assets.
n.3: Guardians have no power to amend wills.

12.q: Under the Trustee Act 2000, what must trustees do when investing trust funds?
o: Have regard to the standard investment criteria
Obtain beneficiaries’ consent for every decision
12.w: The Trustee Act 2000 requires trustees to have regard to the standard investment criteria, including suitability and diversification.

n.0: Trustees must act prudently but cannot guarantee returns.
n.1: They are not restricted to government bonds.
n.3: Routine investment decisions do not need beneficiary consent.

12.q: A company's directors keep trading although insolvency is unavoidable. Which statement correctly describes wrongful trading?
o: Directors may be personally liable for continuing to trade
Shareholders become liable once dividends are paid
Creditors are liable for accepting repayment from the company
Auditors are liable for failing to detect the insolvency
12.w: Wrongful trading occurs where directors knew, or ought to have known, there was no reasonable prospect of avoiding insolvency but continued trading, risking personal liability.

n.1: Shareholder liability is limited to unpaid share capital.
n.2: Creditors are not liable for accepting payments.
n.3: Auditors may face negligence claims, not wrongful trading.

12.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
12.q: Why should adviser Sam reassess a client's liquidity needs at each review?
o: Access requirements can change with life events
Liquidity reviews remove the adviser's disclosure duties
12.w: Access needs can change, for example a house purchase or emergency, so portfolios must stay aligned with liquidity requirements.

n.0: Liquidity reduces but does not remove risk.
n.2: Disclosure duties remain.
n.3: Higher returns are not guaranteed.

12.q: What is the FCA’s statutory competition objective designed to achieve?
o: Ensure identical pricing across all firms
12.w: The competition objective promotes effective competition that benefits consumers through choice, innovation and fair pricing.

n.1: Identical pricing would stifle competition.
n.2: Market risk cannot be eliminated.
n.3: Profits are not guaranteed by regulation.

12.q: Which FCA supervisory approach focuses on identifying systemic risks across firms rather than individual misconduct?
12.w: Thematic supervision examines risks across an entire sector or product line, identifying systemic issues beyond one firm.

n.0: Firm-specific supervision targets individual firms.
n.1: Complaints handling sits under DISP.
n.2: Enforcement is distinct from ongoing supervision.

12.q: A client wants a quick gain that may harm his long-term position. Which factor should guide adviser Nia?
o: Picking whichever is easiest to deliver
Balance both, favouring the long term
Choosing the firm's preferred commercial option
12.w: Balancing client needs while favouring long-term interests keeps advice suitable and ethical.

n.0: Short-term profit may harm suitability.
n.1: Ease does not equal ethics.
n.3: Commercial interest cannot override fairness.

12.q: Why might a young consumer prioritise debt repayment over retirement saving?
o: Because pensions are unavailable to young workers
Because dear debt can outweigh early returns
Because budgeting becomes unnecessary once debt is repaid
Because FCA rules prohibit saving while in debt
12.w: Paying down high-interest debt prevents compounding costs that can exceed returns from early retirement saving.

n.0: Young workers can still contribute to pensions.
n.2: Budgeting remains necessary after repayment.
n.3: No FCA rule prohibits saving while indebted.

12.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to prepare for orderly resolution if they fail?
12.w: Fundamental Rule 8 obliges firms to prepare for resolution so that, if they fail, the process is orderly and systemic risk is minimised.

n.1: Fundamental Rule 2 is about diligence.
n.2: Fundamental Rule 3 concerns prudence.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 5 deals with risk management.

12.q: Which UK authority leads on anti-money laundering supervision of financial firms?
12.w: The FCA supervises anti-money laundering compliance for authorised firms under the Money Laundering Regulations.

n.0: The PRA focuses on prudential safety, not AML.
n.1: The SFO prosecutes serious fraud, not AML supervision.
n.3: The MPC sets monetary policy, not AML rules.

12.q: Which FCA Principle requires firms to manage their business responsibly with adequate risk management systems?
12.w: Principle 3 requires firms to organise and control their affairs responsibly with adequate risk management systems.

n.0: Principle 2 covers skill, care and diligence.
n.2: Principle 5 covers market conduct.
n.3: Principle 8 concerns conflicts of interest.

12.q: What is usually regarded as a consumer's first financial priority?
12.w: An emergency fund provides ready liquidity for unexpected costs, forming the foundation of financial resilience before other goals.

n.1: Equities may suit later, but liquidity comes first.
n.2: Speculative assets are too volatile as a first priority.
n.3: Derivatives are complex and unsuitable as an initial need.

12.q: How does the FCA achieve its effective competition objective?
o: Negotiating trade deals for UK firms
12.w: The competition objective focuses on promoting competition in the interests of consumers, ensuring choice, innovation and fair pricing.

n.0: Competition implies varied, not uniform, pricing.
n.1: Excluding entrants would reduce competition.
n.2: Trade deals are a governmental function.

12.q: How does the PRA’s primary objective contribute to financial stability?
o: By setting fiscal targets for HM Treasury
By promoting firms' safety and soundness
By guaranteeing identical returns for savers
12.w: The PRA's primary objective promotes firms' safety and soundness, reducing systemic risk and supporting stability.

n.0: Fiscal targets are HM Treasury's.
n.1: Consumer lending supervision sits mainly with the FCA.
n.3: Regulators do not guarantee returns.

12.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
12.q: Why must adviser Lucy assess both knowledge and experience before approving a complex product transaction?
o: To lift the sales conversion rate
To make the client a professional
12.w: Assessing knowledge and experience satisfies appropriateness rules and helps prevent unsuitable sales.

n.1: not the purpose
n.2: does not change categorisation
n.3: irrelevant to appropriateness

12.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
12.q: Which is a valid reason for an adviser to increase how often a client is reviewed?
o: The firm has upgraded its IT
12.w: When circumstances change quickly, more frequent reviews help keep advice suitable and outcomes fair.

n.0: Firm revenue targets do not set review frequency.
n.1: IT upgrades do not change review needs.
n.3: Fewer meetings may breach suitability duties.

12.q: What outcome requires firms to design products that meet the needs of a specific consumer group?
12.w: The products and services outcome requires firms to design and distribute products for an identified target market.

n.0: Price and value concerns fairness of charges.
n.1: Support covers service quality, not design.
n.2: Understanding relates to communications clarity.

12.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
12.q: A client wants an outcome that his income and savings cannot realistically fund. What should the adviser do?
o: Ignore the client's affordability constraints entirely
Guarantee the objectives will be met
12.w: Where objectives exceed capacity, advisers must prioritise affordability to protect clients, keeping advice realistic and compliant.

n.1: Ignoring affordability breaches suitability.
n.2: Objectives cannot be guaranteed.
n.3: Higher risk worsens affordability problems.

12.q: Which EU measure harmonises rules for packaged retail and insurance-based investment products?
12.w: The PRIIPs Regulation sets disclosure standards for packaged retail and insurance-based investment products to improve comparability.

n.0: The MiFID II Directive governs market conduct, not PRIIPs disclosure.
n.1: The UCITS Directive applies to collective funds, not PRIIPs broadly.
n.3: The Solvency II Directive covers insurers' prudential rules, not disclosure.

12.q: Which UK Act gave statutory effect to ring-fencing of retail and investment banking?
12.w: The Financial Services (Banking Reform) Act 2013 gave statutory effect to ring-fencing, separating retail from riskier investment banking.

n.0: The Financial Services Act 2012 created the FCA and PRA but not ring-fencing.
n.2: The Banking Act 2009 introduced resolution powers, not ring-fencing.
n.3: The Companies Act 2006 governs company law, not ring-fencing.

12.q: What cultural risk arises when leadership excuses 'star performers' who breach conduct rules?
o: Guaranteed long-term profit growth for the firm
Reduced need for any compliance spending
Improved staff morale and higher retention
12.w: Excusing misconduct for performance erodes ethical standards and undermines cultural integrity.

n.0: Misconduct often harms, not guarantees, profit.
n.2: Compliance costs usually rise with tolerated misconduct.
n.3: Morale falls when rules are applied inconsistently.

12.q: Adviser Owen spots exaggerated green claims in his firm's marketing. What is the ethical response?
o: Ignoring it since rivals do the same
Mentioning it verbally to select clients
Continuing to promote it to drive sales
Escalate it for correction via compliance
12.w: Escalation ensures misleading claims are corrected promptly, protecting clients and integrity.

n.0: Market practice does not justify misconduct.
n.1: Verbal disclosure leaves no record.
n.2: Promoting false claims causes harm.

12.q: What is the role of HM Treasury in relation to the FCA and PRA objectives?
o: It sets the regulators' legislative framework
12.w: HM Treasury sets the legislative and policy framework, giving regulators their objectives and ensuring accountability to Parliament.

n.0: Firm supervision is done by the FCA or PRA.
n.1: Disputes are handled by the FOS.
n.3: Interest rates are set by the MPC.

12.q: Which body coordinates with the FCA on serious financial crime and fraud investigations?
12.w: The Serious Fraud Office works alongside the FCA on serious or complex fraud, sharing enforcement expertise.

n.0: The CMA enforces competition law, not fraud.
n.1: The FOS handles complaints, not criminal enforcement.
n.3: The PRA handles prudential supervision, not fraud.

12.q: Which PRA principle requires firms to conduct business in a prudent manner?
12.w: The PRA requires firms to act in a prudent manner, consistent with promoting safety and soundness.

n.0: Consumer protection is an FCA objective.
n.1: Competition is a secondary PRA objective, not a prudence principle.
n.3: Market integrity is an FCA objective.

12.q: Which UK body maintains the consolidated list of financial sanctions targets?
o: HM Treasury's Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation
12.w: HM Treasury's OFSI maintains the UK's consolidated list of individuals and entities under financial sanctions.

n.1: The FCA does not maintain the sanctions list.
n.2: The NCA receives SARs, not sanctions lists.
n.3: The Bank of England no longer holds this role.

12.q: Within the UK, which regulator is responsible for monitoring competition in wholesale financial markets?
12.w: The CMA investigates and enforces competition issues across all markets, including wholesale financial markets.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority enforces conduct rules, not competition law.
n.2: The Prudential Regulation Authority ensures prudential soundness, not competition.
n.3: The Financial Ombudsman Service handles disputes, not market competition.

12.q: Why must manufacturers define target markets under product governance?
o: To ensure good outcomes and avoid harm
To simplify the periodic disclosures given to clients
12.w: Target market definition supports Consumer Duty and PROD by aligning products to needs and preventing foreseeable harm.

n.0: Maximising commission is not the objective.
n.2: Product governance does not bypass suitability.
n.3: Disclosure simplification is not the purpose.

12.q: Adviser Priya reviews four business structures for a client. Which is a separate legal person that can own property and contract in its own name?
o: A sole trader's registered business name
12.w: An LLP has separate legal personality: it can sue, be sued, own assets and contract independently of its members.

n.0: A general partnership has no separate personality; partners contract personally.
n.1: A sole trader and the business are the same legal person.
n.3: Unincorporated associations cannot generally hold property in their own name.

12.q: Where should client money be held to protect consumers?
12.w: CASS requires client money to be segregated in designated accounts so it is protected if the firm fails.

n.0: A trading account commingles funds, breaching segregation.
n.1: A personal trust lacks the prescribed CASS protections.
n.3: A suspense account is a temporary holding, not the safeguarded location.

12.q: Which firm outcome signals compliance limitation?
o: Success is measured by the absence of fines only
Governance embeds fairness into board reviews
Advisers are rewarded for transparency with clients
12.w: Defining success by fines avoided reflects compliance limitation without ethical depth.

n.1: Fairness in reviews reflects ethical governance.
n.2: Ethical dilemmas in training demonstrate ethics.
n.3: Transparency rewards reflect ethical culture.

12.q: Which FCA sanction is designed primarily to damage a firm's reputation as a deterrent?
12.w: Public censure publishes misconduct details, harming reputation to deter without a financial penalty.

n.0: Prohibition orders ban individuals from regulated activities.
n.1: Restitution orders require compensation, not reputational harm.
n.2: Warning notices signal proposed action, not sanctions.

12.q: Which metric best evidences that Principle 6 is being met across a book of life policy business?
12.w: Sustained persistency suggests products meet needs and customers are treated fairly, indicating good outcomes.

n.0: early lapses imply poor outcomes
n.1: upheld complaints indicate failings
n.3: high redress signals customer harm

12.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to have effective risk strategies and risk management systems?
12.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 5 requires firms to have effective risk strategies and risk management systems for their business.

n.0: Rule 2 covers skill, care and diligence.
n.1: Rule 3 concerns organisation and control.
n.3: Rule 4 concerns adequate financial resources.

12.q: What function do investment banks perform that directly supports capital markets?
o: Provide deposit protection to retail customers
Underwrite and advise on securities issuance
Regulate the conduct of financial advisers
12.w: Investment banks help firms and governments raise capital by underwriting securities and advising on issuance and mergers.

n.0: Deposit protection is the role of the FSCS, not investment banks.
n.1: Pension administration is done by specialist firms, not investment banks.
n.3: Conduct regulation is overseen by the FCA, not investment banks.

12.q: What is the PRA’s primary objective under its statutory remit?
o: Eliminate all instances of market abuse
Promote the safety and soundness of firms
12.w: The PRA's primary objective is to promote the safety and soundness of PRA-authorised firms, reducing adverse effects on the system.

n.0: Market abuse is dealt with by FCA enforcement.
n.2: Tax revenue is a fiscal matter, not a regulatory objective.
n.3: Regulators cannot guarantee protection from all losses.

12.q: How do cooling-off rights protect retail consumers?
12.w: Cooling-off rights give consumers a statutory period to cancel a contract without penalty, protecting their decision.

n.0: Returns are not guaranteed by cooling-off rights.
n.1: Normal charges still apply; they are not eliminated.
n.2: Cooling-off allows cancellation, not lifetime advice.

12.q: What is the role of a prohibition order issued by the FCA?
o: To ban individuals from regulated activities
To require firms to compensate their clients
To temporarily suspend a firm's listing
To publish the details of a breach
12.w: A prohibition order bans an individual from carrying out regulated activities where they are not fit and proper.

n.1: Compensation is secured through restitution orders.
n.2: Suspending listings is a separate regulatory tool.
n.3: Publishing breaches is achieved by public censure.

12.q: Which regulator is tasked with supervising the conduct of financial markets and firms?
12.w: The FCA supervises the conduct of markets and firms, focusing on consumer protection, integrity and competition.

n.1: The PRA supervises prudential soundness.
n.2: The FOS resolves disputes.
n.3: The MPC sets interest rates.

12.q: Which leadership decision most undermines a culture of transparency under Principle 11?
o: Proactively sharing emerging regulator concerns with staff
Delaying disclosure of material compliance failures
12.w: Principle 11 requires openness; delaying disclosure of failures breeds secrecy and non-compliance.

n.0: Proactive sharing strengthens transparency.
n.1: Whistleblower protection supports openness.
n.2: Compliance monitoring promotes transparency.

12.q: Which of the following best describes shadow banking?
12.w: Shadow banking involves non-bank intermediaries, such as money market funds and securitisation conduits, that provide credit with lighter regulation.

n.0: Illegal lending is loan sharking, not shadow banking.
n.1: Fiscal transfers are budgetary actions, not shadow banking.
n.2: Monetary operations are run by central banks, not shadow banks.

12.q: Which product best addresses the need for long-term capital growth?
12.w: Equities offer potential for long-term capital growth, though with higher volatility, suiting wealth accumulation.

n.0: Cash deposits are secure but grow little.
n.1: Overdrafts are debt, not investments.
n.3: Credit cards add liabilities, not capital.

12.q: Which FCA principle requires firms to communicate with clients in a way which is clear, fair and not misleading?
12.w: Principle 7 requires firms to pay due regard to clients' information needs and communicate clearly, fairly and without misleading.

n.0: Principle 3 concerns organisation and risk management.
n.2: Principle 5 covers market conduct.
n.3: Principle 11 covers regulator relations.

12.q: Adviser Sam realises a client needs specialist tax input that lies outside his own expertise. Why are effective delegation skills useful in this situation?
o: Delegation guarantees the client higher returns
Some tasks suit specialists or support staff better
Delegation exempts the adviser from Consumer Duty
12.w: Delegation lets advisers focus on core advisory responsibilities while clients still benefit from specialist expertise where appropriate.

n.0: delegation does not guarantee outcomes
n.2: Consumer Duty applies regardless
n.3: accountability always remains with the adviser

12.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
12.q: How should adviser Raj approach a client identified as vulnerable under FCA guidance?
o: Exclude them from all advice services
12.w: Raj should adapt his communication and process so a vulnerable client can make informed decisions and get fair outcomes.

n.1: denies fair access to advice
n.2: vulnerability does not alter categorisation
n.3: may be unsuitable and avoids responsibility

12.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
12.q: Under Consumer Duty, how should adviser Amir demonstrate compliance within his advice process?
o: Favour the products with the highest revenue
Cut back on the suitability reporting
12.w: Consumer Duty requires evidence that products offer fair value and that clients can understand them.

n.0: revenue is secondary to value and understanding
n.1: reporting must clearly evidence compliance
n.2: understanding must be assessed

12.q: Which adviser outcome is a compliance-only indicator?
o: Escalating ethical dilemmas to compliance teams
Proactively updating clients on emerging risks
12.w: Relying only on disclosure templates reflects compliance-driven outcomes rather than ethics.

n.0: Tailored communication reflects ethical ambition.
n.2: Escalating dilemmas shows ethical outcomes.
n.3: Proactive updates reflect ethics.

12.q: What does the FCA’s consumer protection objective require it to secure?
o: The elimination of all consumer risk
An appropriate degree of consumer protection
Universal access to free financial advice
12.w: The consumer protection objective is to secure an appropriate degree of protection for consumers in regulated markets.

n.0: Regulation cannot eliminate all risk.
n.1: Schemes like the FSCS cover specific cases, not all losses.
n.3: Free advice is not a statutory requirement.

12.q: Which party typically holds legal title in a unit trust structure?
12.w: In a unit trust the trustees hold legal title to the assets for unit holders, who have the beneficial interest.

n.0: Investors hold the beneficial, not legal, interest.
n.1: The manager directs investments but holds no title.
n.3: The FCA regulates funds; it holds no title.

12.q: Which FCA Principle requires firms to organise and control their affairs responsibly with adequate risk systems?
12.w: Principle 3 requires firms to organise and control their affairs responsibly and effectively, with adequate risk management systems.

n.1: Principle 1 covers integrity, not systems and controls.
n.2: Principle 2 relates to diligence, not organisation.
n.3: Principle 10 deals with client asset protection, not organisation.

12.q: How does Government policy influence access to housing finance?
o: By setting mortgage interest rates directly
By introducing schemes like Right to Buy
12.w: Schemes such as Right to Buy and shared ownership widen access to housing finance and encourage lending.

n.0: Mortgage rates are set by lenders, not Government.
n.2: Profits are market-driven, not guaranteed.
n.3: Credit scores are produced by agencies, not Government.

12.q: How does Consumer Duty affect post-sale client servicing?
o: Removes the need for post-sale service
12.w: The Duty requires support throughout the product lifecycle so clients can realise the intended benefits.

n.0: Firms cannot disengage after the sale.
n.2: Distributors also share responsibility, not manufacturers only.
n.3: The Duty continues well beyond cooling-off.

12.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
12.q: Why should adviser Nina carry out stress testing on a client's investment recommendation?
o: To avoid preparing any suitability report
To meet the provider's marketing needs
To show the impact of adverse scenarios
12.w: Stress testing illustrates downside risks and helps the client see how scenarios could affect their objectives.

n.0: both are still required
n.1: it is a risk tool, not marketing
n.3: performance cannot be guaranteed

12.q: How does leadership demonstrate commitment to Principle 10 in client asset protection?
o: By ensuring strong governance over custody
By delegating asset protection entirely to others
By suppressing reconciliation failures from the board
By prioritising firm liquidity over client funds
12.w: Principle 10 requires safeguarding client assets; leadership must ensure governance over segregation and reconciliation.

n.1: Delegation does not remove asset accountability.
n.2: Suppressing failures undermines protection.
n.3: Client funds cannot be subordinated to firm liquidity.

12.q: Which statutory objective underpins the FCA’s duty to ensure that markets are transparent and resilient?
12.w: The market integrity objective requires the FCA to protect and enhance confidence in the system, ensuring transparency and resilience.

n.0: Consumer protection safeguards individuals.
n.1: Competition promotes choice.
n.2: Prudential supervision is the PRA's remit.

12.q: Which reporting outcome signals ethics rather than compliance?
o: Reports focus only on penalties avoided
Reports are issued only after intervention
Reports are limited to checklist completion
12.w: Measuring trust and fairness in reports demonstrates an ethical culture beyond the rules.

n.1: Penalties avoided reflect compliance, not ethics.
n.2: Regulator-driven reporting is compliance.
n.3: Checklists indicate compliance limitation.

12.q: Which regulator's principles underpin the obligation to treat customers fairly?
12.w: The FCA's Principles for Businesses underpin the obligation to treat customers fairly across regulated activities.

n.0: The Bank of England oversees monetary stability, not conduct.
n.1: The PRA supervises prudential safety, not TCF conduct.
n.2: The FOS resolves disputes; TCF is a proactive requirement.

12.q: A discharged bankrupt asks which of his debts still remain payable. Which of the following is not written off by bankruptcy?
12.w: Certain debts, including student loans, court fines and child maintenance, survive bankruptcy and remain payable.

n.0: Credit card debts are generally discharged.
n.1: Unsecured personal loans are usually discharged.
n.2: Overdraft balances are unsecured and dischargeable.

12.q: Which FCA rulebook sets out requirements for systems and controls in firms?
12.w: The Senior Management Arrangements, Systems and Controls (SYSC) Sourcebook sets standards for governance and internal control.

n.0: COBS relates to conduct of business.
n.1: CASS covers client money.
n.2: DISP covers complaints.

12.q: How does corporate culture influence a firm's Principle 6 obligations in practice?
o: It ensures capital adequacy ratios improve
It shapes whether customers are treated fairly
It removes any need for external supervision entirely
12.w: Culture shapes behaviour; where fairness is embedded, firms more consistently treat customers fairly under Principle 6.

n.0: capital adequacy is prudential, not cultural
n.1: profitability is not guaranteed by culture
n.3: supervision remains necessary regardless

12.q: Why might protection needs be prioritised before investment growth?
o: Because rules require everyone to buy protection
Because protection replaces the need for savings
Because stability comes before seeking returns
12.w: Adequate cover protects dependants and stability, providing the foundation for later investment growth.

n.0: Protection is not compulsory for all consumers.
n.1: Protection manages risk; it does not generate returns.
n.2: Savings remain necessary alongside protection.

12.q: Why does FSMA require regulators to publish their statutory objectives?
o: To remove the need for scrutiny
12.w: Publishing objectives makes regulators transparent and accountable, subject to scrutiny in delivering their mandates.

n.1: Regulators are not profit-making bodies.
n.2: HM Treasury retains oversight.
n.3: Parliamentary scrutiny remains essential.

12.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
12.q: A client tells his adviser he no longer needs his money for another twenty years. What should the adviser reconsider?
o: His risk appetite and scope for growth
12.w: A longer horizon may allow greater risk and growth opportunities, so strategy should be reassessed while suitability is evidenced.

n.0: No strategy guarantees higher returns.
n.1: Disclosure cannot be removed.
n.3: Review frequency must still match needs.

12.q: A client wants to rescind an investment contract after a salesperson's false statement of fact induced them to enter it. Which doctrine primarily applies?
o: Common mistake making the contract void
12.w: An actionable misrepresentation, a false statement of fact inducing entry, makes the contract voidable, allowing rescission.

n.0: Common mistake voids a contract only in narrow shared-error cases.
n.1: Frustration concerns supervening events after formation.
n.3: Undue influence involves abuse of a trust relationship, not misstatement.

12.q: A client transacts on a self-select basis, but the adviser's comments effectively steer the choice. When is reliance on execution-only inconsistent with Principle 9?
o: Where the discussions amount to advice
Where the client declines a fact-find
Where a risk warning is signed
12.w: If the interaction amounts to advice, the firm must assess suitability under Principle 9 rather than treat the sale as execution-only.

n.1: providing KIDs supports disclosure, not suitability
n.2: declining a fact-find does not remove suitability if advice is given
n.3: a signed warning does not negate suitability duties

12.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
12.q: Client Wendy has just sold her business for a large sum. What is her adviser's responsibility?
o: Ignore it until the annual review
Reclassify her as an institutional client
12.w: A major asset sale changes financial position and goals, so wealth planning, tax and strategy must be reassessed for suitability.

n.0: Reinvestment returns cannot be guaranteed.
n.1: Waiting risks unsuitable advice.
n.2: An asset sale does not change categorisation.

12.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to prepare for the possibility of failure?
12.w: Fundamental Rule 8 requires firms to prepare for resolution, ensuring an orderly process if they fail.

n.1: Fundamental Rule 3 is about prudence.
n.2: Fundamental Rule 4 concerns financial resources.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 5 relates to risk systems.

12.q: What is the purpose of an FCA warning notice?
o: To impose a financial penalty immediately
To ban an individual from regulated activities
To set out proposed enforcement action
To refer a case to the criminal courts
12.w: A warning notice sets out proposed enforcement action, allowing the recipient to make representations before a decision.

n.0: Penalties follow final notices, not the warning stage.
n.1: Bans require a final decision, not a warning notice.
n.3: Criminal cases are referred separately, not via warning notices.
